graph.title: Standalone ATmega328P on a breadboard programmed from an Arduino (ArduinoISP bootloader burning)
notes: The tutorial has several diagrams (bootloader burning, USB-serial upload, and minimal versions without crystal/caps/resistor). This graph models the main bootloader-burning circuit (first image) with crystal, two caps and 10k reset pull-up. The USB-serial upload variant (second image: Arduino microcontroller removed, Arduino TX/RX wired to ATmega pins 2/3, Arduino RESET wired to ATmega pin 1) is not included, since it re-uses the same breadboard and replaces the ISP wires.
ATmega328P placed straddling the centre channel: pins 1-14 in bank b row f at columns 3-16 (pin n at column n+2), pins 15-28 in bank t row e at columns 16 down to 3 (pin p at column 31-p).
ISP wiring per ArduinoISP: D13->SCK (pin 19), D12->MISO (pin 18), D11->MOSI (pin 17), D10->RESET (pin 1). Power: 5V and GND to rails, rails to VCC (7), AVCC (20), GND (8, 22).

Exact breadboard columns/rails for wires, resistor, crystal and capacitors are inferred from the images; the 10k resistor is a pull-up from RESET (pin 1) to +5V. Crystal across XTAL1/XTAL2 (pins 9, 10), each pin with a 22 pF capacitor to GND.
Resistor value 10k is stored as 10000 (ohms); the catalogue crystal-16mhz and capacitor-22pf types are used for crystal and ceramic capacitors (18-22 pF).
